newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ employment stalls, unemployment up in Mar qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ employment stalls, unemployment up in Mar qtr.

text.p: Employment growth stalled and unemployment rose in the March 1997 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
Seasonally-adjusted employment measured by the Household Labour Force Survey fell 0.1 percent in the March quarter, the second consecutive quarterly fall.
On a seasonally adjusted basis there were 1.69 billion people employed in the March quarter, a fall of 1,000 from the previous quarter. Since March 1996 employment has increased 1.1 percent.
March quarter unemployment returned to September 1996 levels, with the seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rising to 6.4 percent (116,000 unemployed) against 5.9 percent in the December quarter.
The changes were largely blamed on the number of women entering and leaving the workforce.
The unemployment rate for males was 6.2 percent and for females 6.7 percent.

Statistics NZ said the recent volatility in the employment series may be linked to the effects of benefit abatement changes introduced in July last year which increased the amount beneficiaries could earn before their benefits were reduced.
That made it difficult to be certain about the firmness of the changes to unemployment levels in the past nine months, the department said.
While the unemployment rate rose to 6.4 percent from 5.9 percent in the December quarter, the rate was only 0.1 of a percentage point higher than in September 1996.
Long term unemployed increased 7.4 percent in the year to March, with 39,400 unemployed for more than 26 weeks in March 1997.

The largest increases in industry employment in the year to March were for business and financial services, up 22,700; community, social and personal services, up 14,000 and transport storage and communication, up 7,400.
The largest decreases were for agriculture, hunting, fishing and forestry, down 16,700, and manufacturing, down 10,900.
